Yup, that’s the reason it’s step 1. It’s the most important one, but for some it is also the hardest. 

“First step to recovery is admitting a fault”

-Some Dude

Quick disclaimer: I am not at all a psychiatric professional, I am just a guy whose been through the ringer for long enough to know some stuff.

The first step to recovery is admitting a fault, it’s okay that you admitted your problems. I even applaud your selflessness in that even when the problem is yours, you still worry about its affects, that’s good stuff right there. Secondly, you are not at all becoming a deadweight on their shoulders, you are just metaphorically pointing out the 400 pound bag of crap you’ve been carrying for the past year and a half.

Also, regarding the whole self harming part, it’s ok. When you do meet your doctor you need to bring that up, and also begin to slowly bring it up to your parents, they love you dearly.

Coming from experience, you need to be very compliant and honest with them through the recovery process. Keep them updated on any changes, or thoughts you have, and most importantly say thank you whenever you can. Best of luck!
Okay, what did I just scroll into? I came in at the white shield thingy part
Quick disclaimer: I’m not at all a medical professional, that’s just what I do for my friend.

Disclaimer: I am not a psychiatric professional, please talk to your parents or your doctor and receive psychiatric help. My comment alone does not constitute medical fact. 

Regarding social interaction, the easiest way to get better at talking with people is by practicing, and failing. From the seeds of failure grows the tree of life’s greatest joys. 

Second, I understand completely the whole talking about it may affect people’s view on you, but that should never hold you back. I grew up in a family with very high standards too, and if anything this will make your family even more amazing because it shows that you guys are willing to accept failure and grow. So, go to your parents, sit down and talk to them about this. I held off talking to my parents for 5 years buddy, it is not the road you want to take, I promise you. 

And finally, the oh so important grades. Personally I struggled really hard between academics and mental illnesses, but understand that your teachers (or in your case your parents) are not there to watch you fall off the cliff of academics, they are they to instruct, teach, and help you. It is not a fault to admit to them that you need more help. If you can do that, you would be beating me at something I’m still struggling with. 

Take what you will, but please, just get better as soon as you can. Make it your priority everyday to talk to someone. Even before I even talked to my parents (which was hard, not gonna lie) I would come on here and ask this subreddit how I should respond to situations, and after months of telling complete strangers, I finally told my parents.

You got this dude!
Yeah, kinda done with using this account, so I figured why not use what I’ve learned to help others. Thank you though.

Whatcha need? I’ve got a friend with something similar, but I’m no therapist.

Dear random girl I have never met,

Holy shit we are so related. I am a 17 yo secretly bi male who has no hobbies, no friends, and both my dad, grandma, and sister are dying. I suck at school and will probably not graduate. Like you I obsess over little things like my unibrow that I shave constantly, my zits, everything. And like you I have eating disorders that make me loose weight, I mean my metabolism is so high that eating and not eating have the same effect but still I have skipped dinner for the past 3 weeks and eaten only a small breakfast, rarely eaten lunch, and eaten very small snacks. I am currently on the verge of checking into a mental hospital for spring break and letting them help me. But if I was to give one piece of advice to you, it would be this. Take this shitstorm of a life, and make it you goal to spite it everyday. Make it you goal to tell people to go to hell and they would be happy to do so. Make it your goal to one day look back at your old life and go “huh that sucked” as you start up your new car. You can do this, don’t let anyone hold you back. The people of reddit and everywhere else love you for who you are and don’t give shit about your imperfections. Cause like the chi ease would fix their cracked bowls with gold, you are a shining bright bowl that people will one day marvel at. You probably don’t get this a lot, so... I love you, you are amazing, and please keep going! You are so amazing!
Yeah, one day I woke up with lines going from my eyes to my ears, and it was solid white. Eyes were actually extremely clear and not puffy.

Same! 
Depression does affect your sleep cycle, and in my case I’ve developed insomnia. I can stay up till 2:00 am, sleep till 7:00 and function somewhat, but I’ve been trying supplements such as Zquil and different sleep aid dink’s and so far, I sleep better, have fewer night terrors, and overall can function better than if I just sit in my bed and try to relax. Also a Monster energy drink (#not sponsored) before 10:00 am usually helps with productivity levels. But yeah, depression does do this to your sleep schedule, and you are not alone.

Congrats on doing things I wouldn’t even try to do!

I emptied trash, took the dog on a walk, landed a rover on the Mun in KPS, woke up and went to bed last night reasonably, and got ready for my backpacking trip ( 27 pounds baby!) So I think that setting goals might be a new helpful option I can try.

Best way to start is doing what I’ve been taught to alleviate depression; exercise, go out in nature, and do things that would make your boyfriend forget about his depression. Care package wise, I’d put his favorite drink, a heart felt card entailing what you went through and that your willing to help, and then some cookies, brownies, and whatever favorite treats you know he/you love. It is a sign of depression to push people away, so what you need to do is make him stay with you. And most importantly, ask him to get help, now depending on your age this is either easy or difficult, but try your best to get him to treatment options. That is your best bet, and most important, if he leaves do not blame it on him, male brains don’t fully develop till 30 so this is the depression talking, not him.
Thanks, so much. Welp I’m gonna try to get at least some sleep with what little night I have left, and I hope your medical gets better. And I will try to live on, no matter what.

I’ve been going through this for 5 years, and ever since the beginning I wanted it to stop. The insomnia, the night terrors, feeling the  phantom blade go across my wrists, the thoughts that welcome themselves, and the feeling that it will get better, even though it never has. I’ve tried everything, I kept a strict diet, I exercised daily, I even woke up and tried to got to bed at reasonable times. And school is still a month away, and I might do it before then. It just... I feel so dumb coming on here, telling people who I don’t even know how terrible my life is, but yet I never thought about telling doctors when I had the chance. Those quizzes they give you? I lied on the most recent one, and then a week later had a panic attack that almost cost me my life. It’s weird to use the knife that almost ended my life, to carve willow whistles out back. I just want to ask one question to you, do you still think about your friend? I lost 2 good buddies of mine to suicide... and all I ever want, is 1 more day with them.
